description: A regional people director must finalize recognition for a difficult client-transition effort, including the award recipient, the form of recognition, and follow-up commitments for the people involved.

shared_context.S1: The Northstar client transition finished last week after several tense handoffs between the implementation and support teams.
shared_context.S2: Elena has authority to finalize the collaboration award and the associated follow-up commitments.
shared_context.S3: Nadia, Omar, and Leah are the three people currently named in the draft recognition packet.
shared_context.S4: The recognition announcement is scheduled for the monthly staff meeting next Friday.
shared_context.S5: Before Elena finalizes the packet, the normal review routine is a round-robin in which each project participant and HR operations partner gives relevant input.

PF1.text: Marcus personally observed Nadia de-escalate three separate tense handoffs during the Northstar transition and document the agreements that allowed work to continue; he mentioned this informally to another teammate, but it has not been submitted as a formal nomination.

PF2.text: Rina spoke with Nadia after the last handoff, and Nadia said that a surprise public speech would worsen her recent panic symptoms; she prefers a written announcement and an optional small gathering, but has not raised this preference with Elena.

PF3.text: Dev heard Elena promise Omar in a hallway conversation that, if he completed the Northstar transition, he would receive a six-week shadowing assignment with the regional service lead; the informal promise was never entered in the packet.

PF4.text: Sofia confirmed with HR policy this week that a person may be publicly named for an award only after written consent, and that the award decision must include a development conversation scheduled within 10 business days; the confirmation is not yet attached to the recognition packet.

acceptance_conditions: Nadia must receive the collaboration award.
The award citation must identify three specific handoff interventions.
Recognition must use a written announcement plus an optional small gathering rather than a surprise speech.
Written consent must be obtained before Nadia is publicly named.
Omar must receive the promised six-week shadowing assignment.
A development conversation must be scheduled within 10 business days.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'development_assignment' and c['target'] == 'Omar' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Marcus's three observed interventions change the recipient to Nadia and change the citation count from an unspecified nomination to exactly three documented handoffs.
Nadia's stated panic-related preference changes the recognition format from a standard surprise speech to a written announcement plus optional small gathering.
Elena's informal promise changes Omar's follow-up from no specified assignment to exactly six weeks of shadowing with a corresponding development-assignment commitment.
The confirmed HR rule changes the packet to require written consent before naming Nadia and a development conversation within exactly 10 business days.
